subject: Probe synchronization, sampling heuristics and service-credit boundary proposal
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acaciahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acaciahealth.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on measurement windows and credit math (RFP ACAC-47)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the initial RFP submission. Our SRE and procurement teams reviewed the SLA appendix and have two areas where we need precise wording before we can proceed:

1) Measurement sync across regions: our architecture will send traffic to endpoints in us-west and us-east. The RFP asks for a single global availability figure. Please clarify how Redwood will synchronize synthetic probe cadences (we run probes every 30s) and how rolling maintenance windows will be attributed across regions.

2) Credit calculation for partial degradations: the draft defines a single threshold for <99.9% = credit. We have specific concerns about partial degradations where token throughput or 95th latency degrades for a subset of routes. How are credits prorated when only a portion of our traffic is impacted?

Could you provide a short worked example showing a 6-hour partial degradation in us-east affecting 40% of our traffic, including the math for crediting? Also, can you attach any sample probe config you recommend for aligning our probes with Redwood’s telemetry?

Looking to get this clarified before our internal scoring call on Friday.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Director, Cloud Procurement
Acacia Health

P.S. Referenced attachment in RFP: Annex A (we attached an example spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Clarification on measurement windows and credit math (RFP ACAC-47)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Karthik (SRE measurement lead) and Lauren (enterprise contracts) so we can give concise, actionable wording you can score.

High-level answers up front:
- Probe sync: we align measurement by UTC-minute windows and support either synchronized probe scheduling (recommended) or an offset-aware aggregation that maps probe timestamps into 1-minute buckets for cross-region rollups. We will include a sample probe YAML (attached).
- Partial degradations / prorated credits: we propose a traffic-weighted crediting formula where credits are scaled by the fraction of affected ingress (per-customer routing table) and time-in-state. Below I ask Karthik to include a worked example and suggested contract language.

Next steps: Karthik — can you draft the formula and a worked example (6-hour partial in us-east, 40% traffic) and provide suggested SLA text we can include in Annex A? Lauren — once we have the wording, please prepare the minimal legal phrasing to avoid ambiguity (e.g., how maintenance windows are excluded).

Best,
Stephanie
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acaciahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on measurement windows and credit math (RFP ACAC-47)

Hi all — here is the proposed measurement and crediting approach. I'm keeping it tight so you can paste into Annex A.

1) Measurement windows and probe alignment
- Redwood reports availability and latency using aligned UTC 1-minute buckets. Customers can run probes at any cadence; for cross-region aggregation we map probe samples into the minute bucket using the probe timestamp. If customers opt for synchronized probing, we recommend a 30s cadence with randomized jitter <5s to avoid stampeding.
- Rolling maintenance: maintenance events that are scheduled and communicated at least 48 hours in advance are excluded for the specified time windows. Unscheduled maintenance that we initiate to remediate incidents is not excluded, but its impact is subject to standard incident review.

2) Traffic-weighted partial degradation crediting (formula)
- Definitions:
  - T_total = total customer ingress tokens (or requests) across all regions in the measurement window
  - T_impacted = tokens routed to impacted capacity (region/route) during the window
  - Availability_degraded = 1 - (observed_successful_requests_impacted / expected_successful_requests_impacted)
  - Window_factor = fraction_of_time_in_degraded_state (e.g., 6 hours / measurement interval)

- Credit calculation (USD):
  - Base_credit = Monthly_subscription_fee * Service_credit_table[failure_severity]
  - Pro-rated_credit = Base_credit * (T_impacted / T_total) * Window_factor

Worked example (your scenario):
- Assume monthly committed spend = $120,000
- Service_credit_table: 99.9–99.0% -> 10% of monthly fee (example for tiered table in Annex)
- Partial event: 6-hour degradation in us-east; impacts 40% of customer tokens during that time; measurement window = calendar month.

Window_factor = 6 hours / (30 days * 24 hours) = 6 / 720 = 0.008333
T_impacted/T_total = 0.40
Base_credit = $120,000 * 10% = $12,000
Pro-rated_credit = $12,000 * 0.40 * 0.008333 = $40.00 (rounded)

Interpretation: for a narrow, short partial degradation that affects a minority of traffic the resulting credit is small — the proration ensures credits scale with real customer impact rather than a full-month full-service outage credit. This is intentionally conservative and matches our current enterprise practice.

3) Attribution and verification steps
- Redwood will provide: probe timestamps, per-region success/failure rates, routing fraction history (sampled), and incident timeline for the affected period.
- Customer may request a joint review session within 30 days of the event; any adjustments to credits after forensic review will be by mutual agreement with documented evidence.

4) Suggested Annex A wording (short form you can paste):
"During any calendar month, the Customer's Service Credit for partial degradations will be calculated using a traffic-weighted and time-proportional proration. Redwood will compute the fraction of Customer traffic affected and multiply the base Service Credit percentage for the applicable availability tier by the impacted traffic fraction and the fraction of the measurement window during which the degradation persisted. Maintenance events scheduled with >=48 hours notice are excluded from measurement. Forensic telemetry will be provided on request to validate attribution."

Attachments: I attached probe-config-example.yaml (sample probe with timestamping and jitter recommendations) and a one-line sample spreadsheet. Happy to iterate on the exact numeric thresholds if Acacia requires a different credit scale.

—Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acaciahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on measurement windows and credit math (RFP ACAC-47)

Hi Marta — following up with a concise summary and proposed next steps so your scoring committee has an action item list: 

Summary (key points you can paste into your RFP scorecard):
- Measurement: Redwood uses UTC-aligned 1-minute buckets; probes map into those buckets. Synchronized probing at 30s cadence with <5s jitter recommended.
- Crediting: Service credits are traffic-weighted and time-proportional. Example calculation included (result for a 6-hour, 40% traffic impact is ~$40 on a $120k committed month).
- Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance with >=48h notice excluded. Unscheduled corrective maintenance included and reviewed.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide per-region probe results, routing fraction history, and incident timeline. Joint forensic review available within 30 days.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll revise Annex A to include the short-form wording Karthik proposed and send an editable Exhibit to Marta by end of day Thursday.
2) Offer a 60-minute technical workshop (SRE + Procurement) to walk through probe sync and run a small synthetic test against a staging endpoint (we will provide a staging probe config). Requested dates: May 24 or May 26.
3) If Acacia prefers different credit scale midpoints (e.g., 5%/15%/25% tiers instead of the proposed table) tell us and we’ll produce an alternative Annex showing impact on example events.

Attached: RFP_SLA_Annex_A.xlsx (draft Annex with the formula and sample tiers), probe-config-example.yaml.

Would you like us to send the editable Annex directly into your procurement workspace (we can also upload to the Drive link you shared)?

Thanks,
Stephanie
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
